title: Calories: The Reason You're Not Losing Weight (8 Ways To Eat Less)
hook: If you can't lose weight, it usually comes down to one thing: calories. I'll show you the proof, then 8 ways to eat less without being hungry all day.
body: A professor lost 27 pounds eating Twinkies under 1,800 calories a day. Stanford's low-carb vs low-fat study showed both groups losing the same weight. And people who swore they barely ate were eating 47% more than they thought.
close: Save this for the next time you're stuck. Subscribe so you don't miss the next video, where I show you when calories don't matter.
youtube_description:
If you're struggling to lose weight, there's usually one reason: you're eating too many calories. Here is the proof from the real studies, then 8 ways to eat less without being hungry all day.

See what you'd look like with a six-pack, free:
https://absbyai.com/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=longform&utm_content=ro10-calories-not-losing-weight

In this video:
- The professor who lost 27 pounds eating Twinkies, Doritos and Oreos under 1,800 calories a day
- Stanford's low-carb vs low-fat study, where both groups lost about the same weight
- Why people who swear they barely eat were eating 47% more than they thought
- 8 ways to eat less: a GLP-1 medication, know your calorie number, track with AI, fast until 2 PM, black coffee, a salad first, protein snacks, and no liquid calories

I'm not a doctor and this is not medical advice. Talk to your doctor before starting any medication.

Studies mentioned:
- Haub, Kansas State University, 2010 (the Twinkie diet)
- Gardner et al., DIETFITS trial, JAMA, 2018 (Stanford, low-carb vs low-fat)
- Hall and Guo, Gastroenterology, 2017 (controlled-feeding studies)
- Lichtman et al., New England Journal of Medicine, 1992 (reported vs actual calorie intake)
- Jastreboff et al., SURMOUNT-1, New England Journal of Medicine, 2022
- Rolls et al., Journal of the American Dietetic Association, 2004 (salad before a meal)
- DiMeglio and Mattes, International Journal of Obesity, 2000 (liquid vs solid calories)

Some clips in this video are AI-generated, and they're labeled on screen.
